scope: Theorem 1.2 (Lacey–Li) of the manuscript “A uniform Hilbert transform estimate for Lipschitz directions” (preprints/A-uniform-Hilbert-transform-estimate-for-Lipschitz-directions-September-25-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 083 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 38d5c48b4d835003), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 6. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The manuscript presents this as a result of other work, which it uses; the attribution names that work in the manuscript's own words. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let v : R2 → S1 be Lipschitz and 0 < δ < 1. Restrict to rectangles satisfying L(R) ≤ 1 100 Lip(v) , R ∩ v−1 (EX(R)) ≥ δ |R| , where the first restriction is void when Lip(v) = 0. Then Mv,δh(z) = sup R 1R(z) |R| Z R |h| satisfies ∥Mv,δh∥L2,∞ ≤ Cδ−1/2 ∥h∥2 . Here the supremum is tested at every point of R, and the constant is independent of v and δ.
